{"ok": true, "path": "solvers/deutils.py", "start_line": 134, "end_line": 273, "total_lines": 273, "truncated": false, "content": "134:def _desolve(eq, func=None, hint="default", ics=None, simplify=True, *, prep=True, **kwargs):
135:    """This is a helper function to dsolve and pdsolve in the ode
136:    and pde modules.
137:
138:    If the hint provided to the function is "default", then a dict with
139:    the following keys are returned
140:
141:    'func'    - It provides the function for which the differential equation
142:                has to be solved. This is useful when the expression has
143:                more than one function in it.
144:
145:    'default' - The default key as returned by classifier functions in ode
146:                and pde.py
147:
148:    'hint'    - The hint given by the user for which the differential equation
149:                is to be solved. If the hint given by the user is 'default',
150:                then the value of 'hint' and 'default' is the same.
151:
152:    'order'   - The order of the function as returned by ode_order
153:
154:    'match'   - It returns the match as given by the classifier functions, for
155:                the default hint.
156:
157:    If the hint provided to the function is not "default" and is not in
158:    ('all', 'all_Integral', 'best'), then a dict with the above mentioned keys
159:    is returned along with the keys which are returned when dict in
160:    classify_ode or classify_pde is set True
161:
162:    If the hint given is in ('all', 'all_Integral', 'best'), then this function
163:    returns a nested dict, with the keys, being the set of classified hints
164:    returned by classifier functions, and the values being the dict of form
165:    as mentioned above.
166:
167:    Key 'eq' is a common key to all the above mentioned hints which returns an
168:    expression if eq given by user is an Equality.
169:
170:    See Also
171:    ========
172:    classify_ode(ode.py)
173:    classify_pde(pde.py)
174:    """
175:    if isinstance(eq, Equality):
176:        eq = eq.lhs - eq.rhs
177:
178:    # preprocess the equation and find func if not given
179:    if prep or func is None:
180:        eq, func = _preprocess(eq, func)
181:        prep = False
182:
183:    # type is an argument passed by the solve functions in ode and pde.py
184:    # that identifies whether the function caller is an ordinary
185:    # or partial differential equation. Accordingly corresponding
186:    # changes are made in the function.
187:    type = kwargs.get('type', None)
188:    xi = kwargs.get('xi')
189:    eta = kwargs.get('eta')
190:    x0 = kwargs.get('x0', 0)
191:    terms = kwargs.get('n')
192:
193:    if type == 'ode':
194:        from sympy.solvers.ode import classify_ode, allhints
195:        classifier = classify_ode
196:        string = 'ODE '
197:        dummy = ''
198:
199:    elif type == 'pde':
200:        from sympy.solvers.pde import classify_pde, allhints
201:        classifier = classify_pde
202:        string = 'PDE '
203:        dummy = 'p'
204:
205:    # Magic that should only be used internally.  Prevents classify_ode from
206:    # being called more than it needs to be by passing its results through
207:    # recursive calls.
208:    if kwargs.get('classify', True):
209:        hints = classifier(eq, func, dict=True, ics=ics, xi=xi, eta=eta,
210:        n=terms, x0=x0, hint=hint, prep=prep)
211:
212:    else:
213:        # Here is what all this means:
214:        #
215:        # hint:    The hint method given to _desolve() by the user.
216:        # hints:   The dictionary of hints that match the DE, along with other
217:        #          information (including the internal pass-through magic).
218:        # default: The default hint to return, the first hint from allhints
219:        #          that matches the hint; obtained from classify_ode().
220:        # match:   Dictionary containing the match dictionary for each hint
221:        #          (the parts of the DE for solving).  When going through the
222:        #          hints in "all", this holds the match string for the current
223:        #          hint.
224:        # order:   The order of the DE, as determined by ode_order().
225:        hints = kwargs.get('hint',
226:                           {'default': hint,
227:                            hint: kwargs['match'],
228:                            'order': kwargs['order']})
229:    if not hints['default']:
230:        # classify_ode will set hints['default'] to None if no hints match.
231:        if hint not in allhints and hint != 'default':
232:            raise ValueError("Hint not recognized: " + hint)
233:        elif hint not in hints['ordered_hints'] and hint != 'default':
234:            raise ValueError(string + str(eq) + " does not match hint " + hint)
235:        # If dsolve can't solve the purely algebraic equation then dsolve will raise
236:        # ValueError
237:        elif hints['order'] == 0:
238:            raise ValueError(
239:                str(eq) + " is not a solvable differential equation in " + str(func))
240:        else:
241:            raise NotImplementedError(dummy + "solve" + ": Cannot solve " + str(eq))
242:    if hint == 'default':
243:        return _desolve(eq, func, ics=ics, hint=hints['default'], simplify=simplify,
244:                      prep=prep, x0=x0, classify=False, order=hints['order'],
245:                      match=hints[hints['default']], xi=xi, eta=eta, n=terms, type=type)
246:    elif hint in ('all', 'all_Integral', 'best'):
247:        retdict = {}
248:        gethints = set(hints) - {'order', 'default', 'ordered_hints'}
249:        if hint == 'all_Integral':
250:            for i in hints:
251:                if i.endswith('_Integral'):
252:                    gethints.remove(i[:-len('_Integral')])
253:            # special cases
254:            for k in ["1st_homogeneous_coeff_best", "1st_power_series",
255:                "lie_group", "2nd_power_series_ordinary", "2nd_power_series_regular"]:
256:                if k in gethints:
257:                    gethints.remove(k)
258:        for i in gethints:
259:            sol = _desolve(eq, func, ics=ics, hint=i, x0=x0, simplify=simplify, prep=prep,
260:                classify=False, n=terms, order=hints['order'], match=hints[i], type=type)
261:            retdict[i] = sol
262:        retdict['all'] = True
263:        retdict['eq'] = eq
264:        return retdict
265:    elif hint not in allhints:  # and hint not in ('default', 'ordered_hints'):
266:        raise ValueError("Hint not recognized: " + hint)
267:    elif hint not in hints:
268:        raise ValueError(string + str(eq) + " does not match hint " + hint)
269:    else:
270:        # Key added to identify the hint needed to solve the equation
271:        hints['hint'] = hint
272:    hints.update({'func': func, 'eq': eq})
273:    return hints"}

821:def classify_ode(eq, func=None, dict=False, ics=None, *, prep=True, xi=None, eta=None, n=None, **kwargs):
822:    r"""
823:    Returns a tuple of possible :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve`
824:    classifications for an ODE.
825:
826:    The tuple is ordered so that first item is the classification that
827:    :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve` uses to solve the ODE by default.  In
828:    general, classifications at the near the beginning of the list will
829:    produce better solutions faster than those near the end, thought there are
830:    always exceptions.  To make :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve` use a
831:    different classification, use ``dsolve(ODE, func,
832:    hint=<classification>)``.  See also the
833:    :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve` docstring for different meta-hints
834:    you can use.
835:
836:    If ``dict`` is true, :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.classify_ode` will
837:    return a dictionary of ``hint:match`` expression terms. This is intended
838:    for internal use by :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve`.  Note that
839:    because dictionaries are ordered arbitrarily, this will most likely not be
840:    in the same order as the tuple.
841:
842:    You can get help on different hints by executing
843:    ``help(ode.ode_hintname)``, where ``hintname`` is the name of the hint
844:    without ``_Integral``.
845:
846:    See :py:data:`~sympy.solvers.ode.allhints` or the
847:    :py:mod:`~sympy.solvers.ode` docstring for a list of all supported hints
848:    that can be returned from :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.classify_ode`.
849:
850:    Notes
851:    =====
852:
853:    These are remarks on hint names.
854:
855:    ``_Integral``
856:
857:        If a classification has ``_Integral`` at the end, it will return the
858:        expression with an unevaluated :py:class:`~.Integral`
859:        class in it.  Note that a hint may do this anyway if
860:        :py:meth:`~sympy.core.expr.Expr.integrate` cannot do the integral,
861:        though just using an ``_Integral`` will do so much faster.  Indeed, an
862:        ``_Integral`` hint will always be faster than its corresponding hint
863:        without ``_Integral`` because
864:        :py:meth:`~sympy.core.expr.Expr.integrate` is an expensive routine.
865:        If :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve` hangs, it is probably because
866:        :py:meth:`~sympy.core.expr.Expr.integrate` is hanging on a tough or
867:        impossible integral.  Try using an ``_Integral`` hint or
868:        ``all_Integral`` to get it return something.
869:
870:        Note that some hints do not have ``_Integral`` counterparts. This is
871:        because :py:func:`~sympy.integrals.integrals.integrate` is not used in
872:        solving the ODE for those method. For example, `n`\th order linear
873:        homogeneous ODEs with constant coefficients do not require integration
874:        to solve, so there is no
875:        ``nth_linear_homogeneous_constant_coeff_Integrate`` hint. You can
876:        easily evaluate any unevaluated
877:        :py:class:`~sympy.integrals.integrals.Integral`\s in an expression by
878:        doing ``expr.doit()``.
879:
880:    Ordinals
881:
882:        Some hints contain an ordinal such as ``1st_linear``.  This is to help
883:        differentiate them from other hints, as well as from other methods
884:        that may not be implemented yet. If a hint has ``nth`` in it, such as
885:        the ``nth_linear`` hints, this means that the method used to applies
886:        to ODEs of any order.
887:
888:    ``indep`` and ``dep``
889:
890:        Some hints contain the words ``indep`` or ``dep``.  These reference
891:        the independent variable and the dependent function, respectively. For
892:        example, if an ODE is in terms of `f(x)`, then ``indep`` will refer to
893:        `x` and ``dep`` will refer to `f`.
894:
895:    ``subs``
896:
897:        If a hints has the word ``subs`` in it, it means that the ODE is solved
898:        by substituting the expression given after the word ``subs`` for a
899:        single dummy variable.  This is usually in terms of ``indep`` and
900:        ``dep`` as above.  The substituted expression will be written only in
901:        characters allowed for names of Python objects, meaning operators will
902:        be spelled out.  For example, ``indep``/``dep`` will be written as
903:        ``indep_div_dep``.
904:
905:    ``coeff``
906:
907:        The word ``coeff`` in a hint refers to the coefficients of something
908:        in the ODE, usually of the derivative terms.  See the docstring for
909:        the individual methods for more info (``help(ode)``).  This is
910:        contrast to ``coefficients``, as in ``undetermined_coefficients``,
911:        which refers to the common name of a method.
912:
913:    ``_best``
914:
915:        Methods that have more than one fundamental way to solve will have a
916:        hint for each sub-method and a ``_best`` meta-classification. This
917:        will evaluate all hints and return the best, using the same
918:        considerations as the normal ``best`` meta-hint.
919:
920:
921:    Examples
922:    ========
923:
924:    >>> from sympy import Function, classify_ode, Eq
925:    >>> from sympy.abc import x
926:    >>> f = Function('f')
927:    >>> classify_ode(Eq(f(x).diff(x), 0), f(x))
928:    ('nth_algebraic',
929:    'separable',
930:    '1st_exact',
931:    '1st_linear',
932:    'Bernoulli',
933:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_best',
934:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_subs_indep_div_dep',
935:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_subs_dep_div_indep',
936:    '1st_power_series', 'lie_group', 'nth_linear_constant_coeff_homogeneous',
937:    'nth_linear_euler_eq_homogeneous',
938:    'nth_algebraic_Integral', 'separable_Integral', '1st_exact_Integral',
939:    '1st_linear_Integral', 'Bernoulli_Integral',
940:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_subs_indep_div_dep_Integral',
941:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_subs_dep_div_indep_Integral')
942:    >>> classify_ode(f(x).diff(x, 2) + 3*f(x).diff(x) + 2*f(x) - 4)
943:    ('factorable', 'nth_linear_constant_coeff_undetermined_coefficients',
944:    'nth_linear_constant_coeff_variation_of_parameters',
945:    'nth_linear_constant_coeff_variation_of_parameters_Integral')
946:
947:    """
948:    ics = sympify(ics)
949:
950:    if func and len(func.args) != 1:
951:        raise ValueError("dsolve() and classify_ode() only "
952:        "work with functions of one variable, not %s" % func)
953:
954:    if isinstance(eq, Equality):
